facts: The paper 'Electoral Violence, Partisan Identity, and Perceptions of Election Quality: A Survey Experiment in West Bengal, India' was written by Ursula Daxecker and Hanne Fjelde.
The article was published on 2022-10-01 in Comparative Politics.
The study examines the consequences of election violence for citizens' political attitudes in polarized contexts.
The authors used a vignette experiment conducted in West Bengal following India's 2019 elections, varying the partisan identity of the perpetrator of violence.

The paper argues that when presented with information alleging co-partisans' involvement in violence, people with strong partisan identities become more likely to assert that elections were free and fair.
Supporters of the Trinamool Congress (TMC) increased their evaluations of election quality when presented with information about co-partisan violence.
No evidence of disconfirmation bias was found for Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) supporters.
The authors plausibly explain the lack of disconfirmation bias among BJP supporters by their recent shift to the party.
